technique: Textbook PINN: MLP on the 9 raw contract inputs plus a put flag; Heston PDE residual in (S, v, tau) on the training box; soft payoff loss; Adam
Exact reduction to (x, v, tau) and (kappa, theta, xi, rho); driftless reduced PDE; put-call parity; far x boundary at the Black-Scholes base
Hard terminal condition: c = BS(x, w tau) + tau N(x, v, sqrt(tau), kappa, theta, xi, rho) with w the expected average variance, so the payoff holds exactly and the network learns the correction
Loss balancing: residual weighted by tau / tau_max against the 1/sqrt(tau) blow-up at the strike, with collocation tau = tau_max u^2

Variance boundary (new): the degenerate PDE c_tau = kappa theta c_v as a residual on v = 0; v extended to v_hi = 3 with c_v = 0 there (moves interior prices by at most 4e-7, results/neural/variance_cap_study); collocation packed near v = 0 (v = v_hi u^2) and sqrt(v + 0.01) as the network input
Residual-based adaptive sampling (RAD): every 1000 steps keep 32,768 of 131,072 candidates drawn with probability proportional to |residual| / mean + 1
Quasi-Newton polish: full-batch L-BFGS (strong Wolfe line search) warm-started from P5 on 16,384 RAD-selected collocation points
Second-order refinement: Nystrom-preconditioned Newton-CG (Rathore et al., 2024) warm-started from P6
Scale up: width 128 and 25,000 Adam steps from a fresh start, then 1,000 L-BFGS iterations and 20 Newton-CG steps
stopped_early: adam stopped at step 19200 of 25000: wall-clock cap

technique: Enveloped correction as an implied-volatility output: c = BS(x, sqrt(w tau) e^N), whose first-order correction sqrt(w tau) phi(d_2) N fades like the time value near expiry and away from the strike, with kappa and theta fed as kappa tau and kappa theta tau so that their effect vanishes as tau -> 0 (two earlier variants are reported: the additive tau phi(d_2) N envelope, and the implied-volatility output with plain kappa, theta inputs); trained from a fresh start through the Adam, L-BFGS and Newton-CG stages
Anchored (hybrid) PINN: fine-tune P9 with the PDE residual plus reference prices at 4,096 anchor contracts of the training domain (their own seed), then L-BFGS
Textbook DeepONet: branch on (r, q, kappa, theta, xi, rho) plus a put flag, trunk on (S/K, v0, tau); price labels from the reference; Adam
Exact reduction: branch on (kappa, theta, xi, rho), trunk on (x, v, tau); put-call parity
Black-Scholes at the expected average variance as the base: c = BS + tau <branch, trunk(x, v, sqrt(tau))>
Differential (Sobolev) training: add the 10 derivative labels c_x, c_v, c_tau, c_kappa, c_theta, c_xi, c_rho, c_xx, c_xv, c_vv

Physics-informed DeepONet: PDE residual on unlabelled collocation over the computational box (tau from 0, v to v_hi = 3 packed near 0, sqrt(v + 0.01) in the trunk), the degenerate equation on v = 0, c_v = 0 at v_hi and the far x boundary
Short maturities: 25% of the labelled contracts and of the collocation drawn with tau in 0.005 to 0.05
Quasi-Newton polish: full-batch L-BFGS warm-started from D5 on 4,096 labelled contracts and 4,096 collocation points
Scale up: width and rank 128 and 131,072 labelled contracts from a fresh start, then the L-BFGS stage of D6

Enveloped correction as an implied-volatility output: c = BS(x, sqrt(w tau) e^N), whose first-order correction fades like the time value near expiry and away from the strike, with a drift split N = <branch(xi, rho), trunk_1> + (tau / tau_max) <branch(kappa, theta, xi, rho), trunk_2> so that kappa and theta drop out as tau -> 0 (the implied-volatility output without the split is reported as a variant); trained from a fresh start through the Adam and L-BFGS stages
Ensemble: average of four independently seeded D8 trainings (seeds 0-3); Greeks are member averages
